qso-courtesy.title: A good neighbour
qso-courtesy.prompt: Choose what you'd do at each turn.

config.setting: 80 m, Tuesday evening. You want to check in to the 3.760 MHz net.

turns.situation: You've just switched on the radio. What do you do first?

options.text: Listen to make sure the frequency isn't in use
Ask "Is this frequency in use?" straight away
options.feedback: Listen first. Asking can still interrupt someone you couldn't hear yet.

options.text: Turn up the power so you'll be heard
options.feedback: More power doesn't come first; listening does.

turns.situation: You need to adjust your antenna tuner before checking in to the net on 3.760.

options.feedback: 1 kHz is right on top of the net's audio. Go 3 to 5 kHz away.
Never tune up on top of a net.

turns.situation: After the net, a local station says you're 20 dB over S9.

options.text: Turn the power down to what's needed

options.feedback: You're already very strong. Use less power.

turns.situation: You're chatting on 3.745 when someone says a net starts here in five minutes.

options.text: Keep talking; you were here first
options.feedback: As a courtesy, move. No one owns a frequency.

turns.situation: Later, propagation changes and another contact starts bleeding over yours.

options.feedback: Listen first, power down, and move when you need to. That's good operating.

options.text: Tell them to move, since you were first
options.feedback: No one owns a frequency. The easy fix is to move.
That only makes it worse for everyone.

qso-courtesy.success: Listen first, power down, and move when you need to. That's good operating.
